arabic: وَجَمَ الأَوْلَادُ العُودَ فِي الجَنَّةِ ثُمَّ فَطَرَ العَامِلُ العُودَ بِالفَاسِ.
english: The boys gathered the wood in the garden, then the worker split it with the axe.
reason: وَجَمَ does not mean 'gathered'; use جَمَعَ. العود also denotes a stick or piece of wood here. See the [Arabic Academy dictionary](https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/وجم).

arabic: انْتَشَرَ الجُدَرِيُّ فِي المِنْطَقَةِ ثُمَّ وَجَمَ المُمَرِّضُ الأَطْفَالَ فِي القَاعَةِ.
english: Smallpox spread in the area, then the nurse gathered the children in the hall.
reason: وَجَمَ الأطفالَ does not mean 'gathered the children'; جَمَعَ الأطفالَ is required.

arabic: نَوَّعَ الطَّاهِي الطَّعَامَ فِي المَأْدُبَةِ ثُمَّ وَجَمَ الأَطْبَاقَ فِي القَاعَةِ.
english: The cook diversified the food at the feast, then collected the plates in the hall.
reason: وَجَمَ الأطباقَ does not mean 'collected the plates'; use جَمَعَ الأطباقَ.

arabic: فَطَرَ الوَالِدُ البُرْتُقَالَ لِلْأَطْفَالِ ثُمَّ نَوَّعَ العَصِيرَ أَيْضًا بِالمَوْزِ.
english: The father split the oranges for the children, then also varied the juice with bananas.
reason: Unusual wording, but splitting oranges and varying juice by adding bananas describe a plausible scene. The English matches.

arabic: سَمِعَ الطُّلَّابُ مَقْطَعًا مِنْ مُقَابَلَةِ خَبِيرٍ قَمَرِيٍّ فِي المَعْهَدِ.
english: The students heard a passage from an interview with a Comorian expert at the institute.
reason: A coherent, grammatical sentence about listening to an interview excerpt. قمري can denote Comorian.

arabic: شَاهَ الزَّهْرُ فِي العَاصِفَةِ، لَكِنَّهُ جَذَّرَ مِنْ جَدِيدٍ فِي الرَّبِيعِ.
english: The flowers were damaged in the storm, but they took root again in the spring.
reason: جَذَّرَ is transitive, meaning to establish or root something; 'took root' requires تَجَذَّرَ here. See [Riyadh Dictionary](https://dictionary.ksaa.gov.sa/result/جَذَّرَ).

arabic: المُؤَلِّفُ قَمَرِيٌّ، وَهَذَا المَقْطَعُ مِنْ كِتَابِهِ مَشْهُورٌ جِدًّا.
english: The author is Comorian, and this passage from his book is very famous.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; the translation accurately conveys the author's nationality and the passage's fame.

arabic: شَاهَ هَذَا المَقْطَعُ فِي التَّرْجَمَةِ الجَدِيدَةِ، فَرَاجَعَهُ المُعَلِّمُ وَالطُّلَّابُ فَوْرًا.
english: This passage came out badly in the new translation, so the teacher and the students reviewed it immediately.
reason: شاهَ is uncommon but valid for becoming marred or ugly, including figuratively in translation. The English captures this. See the [Arabic Academy dictionary](https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/شوه).

arabic: حَرَثَ الْعَامِلُ الْأَرْضَ مِنَ الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى التَّاسِعَةِ، ثُمَّ انْصَرَفَ.
english: The worker plowed the ground from morning until nine o'clock, then left.
reason: A natural description of work lasting from the morning until nine, followed by departure.

arabic: شَفَى الطَّبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ فِعْلًا مِنَ الِالْتِهَابِ الْكَبِيرِ فِي جَبْهَتِهِ.
english: The doctor really did heal the boy of the big inflammation on his forehead.
reason: The wording is somewhat stiff, but the sentence is grammatical and describes a plausible recovery. The English matches.

arabic: شَفَى اللّهُ الْعَمَّ مِنَ الْمَرَضِ، ثُمَّ حَرَثَ الْأَرْضَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
english: God healed the uncle of his illness, and then he plowed the ground in the morning.
reason: The uncle can naturally be understood as the subject of حرث after his recovery. The English preserves this reading.

arabic: فِي التَّاسِعَةِ صَبَاحًا قَدَّمَ الْوَزِيرُ إِعْلَانًا هَامًّا عَنِ الْجَبْهَةِ.
english: At nine in the morning, the minister made an important announcement about the front.
reason: A grammatical, plausible announcement about a military front, accurately translated.

arabic: أَخِي نَباتِيٌّ، فَقَدْ كَرِهَ اللَّحْمَ وَالهَمْبَرْجَرَ وَالشِّيش طَوَالَ سِنِينٍ.
english: My brother is a vegetarian; he has disliked meat, hamburgers, and skewers for years.
reason: A plausible statement about a vegetarian’s longstanding dislike of meat dishes; the translation matches.

arabic: الطِّفْلُ كَرِهَ الزَّنْجَبِيلَ فِي الشَّايِ، فَطَحَنَ لَهُ العَمُّ القِرْفَةَ.
english: The child disliked the ginger in the tea, so his uncle ground cinnamon for him.
reason: A coherent situation in which cinnamon is prepared as an alternative flavoring. The translation is accurate.

arabic: كَرِهَ العَمُّ أَنْ أَسْأَلَهُ هُنَا عَنْ مُوَلِّدِهِ فِي لُبْنَانَ.
english: My uncle disliked that I asked him here about his birthplace in Lebanon.
reason: مُوَلِّدِهِ means 'his generator,' not 'his birthplace,' which would be مَوْلِدِهِ.

arabic: طَحَنَ الخَبَّازُ القِرْفَةَ وَالسُّكَّرَ لِلْمُوَظَّفِ النَّباتِيِّ فِي المَكْتَبِ الآنَ.
english: The baker ground cinnamon and sugar for the vegetarian employee in the office now.
reason: The preparation and intended recipient are plausible. الآن can refer to an action just completed, although both sentences are slightly awkward.

arabic: اِسْتِضَافَةُ إِعْدَادِيَّةِ القَرْيَةِ لِلِاحْتِفَالِ فِي أَغُسْطُس سَرَّتِ الطَّلَبَةَ كَثِيرًا.
english: The village preparatory school's hosting of the celebration in August pleased the students a lot.
reason: A grammatical, plausible statement about a school hosting a celebration. The translation matches.

arabic: فِي الصَّبَاحِ اِعْتَصَرَ الجَدُّ التُّفَّاحَ ثُمَّ خَلَطَهُ مَعَ عِرْقسُوس.
english: In the morning the grandfather squeezed the apples, then mixed them with licorice.
reason: A plausible description of preparing a fruit drink with licorice. The translation accurately conveys the actions.

arabic: أَحَبَّ طَلَبَةُ إِعْدَادِيَّةِ القَرْيَةِ الشُّوكُولَاتَةَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ عِرْقسُوس فِي الصَّيْفِ.
english: The students of the village preparatory school liked chocolate more than licorice in the summer.
reason: A simple, plausible comparison of students’ preferences. The translation is accurate.

arabic: اِعْتَصَرَ الصَّبِيُّ مِنْ إِعْدَادِيَّةِ القَرْيَةِ ثَمَرًا كَثِيرًا لِلِاحْتِفَالِ فَسَرَّ الطَّلَبَةَ.
english: The boy from the village preparatory school squeezed a lot of fruit for the celebration, which delighted the students.
reason: Preparing fruit juice for a school celebration is coherent, and the translation captures the resulting delight.

arabic: هُنَاكَ طَاوُوقٌ نَاعِمٌ جِدًّا فِي هَذَا المَطْعَمِ، فَالأَطْفَالُ مُغْتَبِطُونَ.
english: There is very tender tawook in this restaurant, so the children are delighted.
reason: ناعم is less idiomatic than طري for tender chicken, but the description and the children’s reaction are plausible.

arabic: جَدِّي رَجُلٌ ذَاكِرٌ وَصَبُورٌ، وَمِزَاجُهُ نَاعِمٌ مَعَ الأَطْفَالِ جَمِيعًا.
english: My grandfather is a mindful and patient man, and his temperament is gentle with all the children.
reason: مزاجه ناعم مع الأطفال is an unnatural expression for treating children gently. ذاكِر means remembering or engaging in remembrance, rather than generally 'mindful.'

arabic: هُنَاكَ طَاوُوقٌ جَاهِزٌ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ، وَالصَّائِمُ ذَاكِرٌ وَصَبُورٌ.
english: There is tawook ready on the table, and the person fasting is mindful and patient.
reason: The Arabic is plausible with ذاكِر referring to someone remembering God, but 'mindful' does not accurately convey that religious activity.

arabic: هَذَا طَاوُوقٌ نَاعِمٌ جِدًّا، وَالسَّلَطَةُ وَالأَرُزُّ جَاهِزَانِ عَلَى الطَّاوِلَةِ.
english: This is very tender tawook, and the salad and rice are ready on the table.
reason: A coherent description of a prepared meal, with correct dual agreement in جاهزان. ناعم is understandable here as soft or tender.

arabic: سَهِرَ المُصَوِّرُ مُنْفَرِدًا فِي المِنْطَقَةِ المُجَاوِرَةِ لِلْبَنْكِ.
english: The photographer stayed up alone in the area next to the bank.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; the translation accurately conveys staying up alone near the bank.

arabic: الجُوعُ قَادَ السُّلَحْفَاةَ إِلَى العُشْبِ الرَّطْبِ.
english: Hunger led the turtle to the moist grass.
reason: A coherent description of a hungry turtle moving toward moist grass; accurately translated.

arabic: حَرَثَ الجَدُّ، فَنَمَا القَمْحُ وَالخَضْرَاوَاتُ فِي الرَّبِيعِ المَاطِرِ.
english: Grandfather plowed, so the wheat and vegetables grew in the rainy spring.
reason: A plausible farming scene with correct grammar and an accurate translation.

arabic: لَيْسَ البَهَارُ المَغْشُوشُ رَخِيصًا، فَشِرَاؤُهُ فَشَلٌ.
english: Adulterated spice is not cheap, so buying it is a failure.
reason: Somewhat blunt phrasing, but calling the purchase of overpriced adulterated spice a failure is coherent and plausible.

arabic: فَحَصَ المُتَخَصِّصُ فِي العِيَادَةِ حَلْقِي وَجَبْهَتِي.
english: The specialist in the clinic examined my throat and my forehead.
reason: A plausible medical examination, correctly expressed and translated.

arabic: طَالَتِ المَسِيرَةُ فِي الشَّارِعِ، لَكِنَّ النَّشِيطِينَ لَوَّحُوا وَصَاحُوا.
english: The march in the street grew long, but the energetic ones waved and shouted.
reason: The contrast between a lengthy march and energetic participants is coherent; the translation matches.

arabic: ذَابَ الشَّمْعُ عَلَى الطَّاقِ، وَلَمَعَ الضِّيَاءُ فِي الجِدَارِ.
english: The wax melted on the arch, and the light gleamed on the wall.
reason: For light gleaming on a wall, Arabic normally uses على الجدار. في الجدار means within the wall and makes the intended scene awkward; the English silently changes this relationship.

arabic: يَاتُرَى مَنْ خَادَعَ ذَلِكَ الشَّخْصَ بِهَذِهِ الحِيلَةِ؟
english: I wonder who deceived that person with this trick?
reason: A plausible question with an accurate translation. يا ترى is conventionally written as two words.

arabic: لَعَلَّ الجَدَّةَ مَبْسُوطَةٌ الآنَ بِالقُدَّاسِ وَبِالذِّكْرَى.
english: Perhaps grandmother is happy now with the mass and the memory.
reason: Grandmother being pleased with a Mass and a particular memory is plausible in context; the translation matches.

arabic: بِذْلَةُ المُحَامِي بُنِّيَّةٌ، وَلِحْيَتُهُ وَحَاجِبُهُ بُنِّيَّانِ أَيْضًا.
english: The lawyer's suit is brown, and his beard and eyebrow are also brown.
reason: Grammatically correct, including masculine dual agreement for the beard and eyebrow together; accurately translated.

arabic: ضَرَبَ الأَبُ الطَّبْلَ بِسَبَّابَتِهِ، فَنَظَرَتِ الجَدَّةُ إِلَيْهِ.
english: The father struck the drum with his index finger, so grandmother looked at him.
reason: Tapping a drum with an index finger is plausible, and the translation is accurate.

arabic: اتَّفَقَ الأَبُ وَالجَدُّ عَلَى المَبْلَغِ، فَأَطَاعَ الحَفِيدُ.
english: The father and grandfather agreed on the amount, so the grandson obeyed.
reason: A coherent family interaction; what the grandson obeyed can be understood from context. The translation is accurate.

arabic: كَرِهَ النَّبَاتِيُّ شَمَّ الطَّاوُوقِ فِي الحَفْلَةِ، فَاسْتَأْذَنَ مُبَكِّراً.
english: The vegetarian hated the smell of tawook at the party, so he asked permission to leave early.
reason: A plausible reaction to food at a party; asking permission to leave is naturally understood from context.

arabic: عَانَى الأَرْمَلُ مِنَ الوَحْدَةِ، فَسَهِرَ وَتَعِبَ جِدّاً.
english: The widower suffered from loneliness, so he stayed up and got very tired.
reason: Grammatical and plausible, with an accurate translation.

arabic: مَقَرُّ الاِتِّحَادِ فِي الطَّابِقِ الرَّابِعِ مِنَ العِمَارَةِ.
english: The union's headquarters is on the fourth floor of the building.
reason: A natural statement about the location of the union's headquarters.

arabic: الاِرْتِفَاعُ فِي مُعَدَّلِ العَجْزِ أَزْمَةٌ فِي الكُوَيْتِ.
english: The rise in the deficit rate is a crisis in Kuwait.
reason: Formal but coherent economic commentary; the translation matches.

arabic: آمَنَ الرَّجُلُ بِالسِّلْمِ، لَكِنَّ العَدُوَّ خَادَعَهُ فِي النِّهَايَةِ.
english: The man believed in peace, but the enemy deceived him in the end.
reason: A coherent narrative statement with an accurate translation.

arabic: فَرَدَ الطَّاوُوسُ رِيشَهُ الفِضِّيَّ، فَدَمْدَمَ البَبَّغَاءُ بِجَانِبِهِ.
english: The peacock spread its silvery feathers, so the parrot muttered next to it.
reason: Plausible descriptive narration, including in a story; silvery plumage and a muttering parrot are acceptable.

arabic: اِقْتَرَحَ المُهَنْدِسُ طَرِيقَةً مُتَطَوِّرَةً لِإِنْقَاذِ العَامِلِ فِي المَغَارَةِ.
english: The engineer proposed an advanced method to rescue the worker in the cave.
reason: A plausible rescue situation, expressed grammatically and translated accurately.

arabic: كَانَ المَوْعِدُ صَبَاحَ الأَحَدِ، لَكِنَّ الوَفْدَ قَدِمَ مُتَأَخِّراً.
english: The appointment was on Sunday morning, but the delegation arrived late.
reason: A natural contrast between the scheduled time and the delegation's late arrival.

arabic: تَعِبَ الطَّالِبُ مِنَ الصِّيَامِ الإِلْزَامِيِّ فِي رَمَضَانَ.
english: The student got tired from the mandatory fasting in Ramadan.
reason: A plausible statement about fatigue during obligatory Ramadan fasting.

arabic: طَحَنَتْ رَبَّةُ الخِبَاءِ العِرْقسُوسَ، ثُمَّ رَخَّتْهُ وَوَزَعَتْهُ.
english: The lady of the tent ground the licorice, then diluted it and distributed it.
reason: An old-fashioned but coherent drink-preparation scene. رَخَّ can mean mixing or diluting a drink: [Arabic Language Academy](https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/رخخ).

arabic: قَابَ القَانِصُ الأَرْضَ بِالفَاسِ، ثُمَّ خَزَنَ الأَكْلَ فِي المَغَارَةِ.
english: The hunter dug the ground with the axe, then stored the food in the cave.
reason: A plausible hunting narrative. The rare verb قابَ means digging a hollow in the ground: [Arabic Language Academy](https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/قوب).

arabic: الوَصِيفُ مَغْرُورٌ، لَكِنَّ نَزَاهَتَهُ وَجِدَّهُ سَاعَدَاهُ فِي المَجَالِ.
english: The young man is arrogant, but his integrity and diligence helped him in the field.
reason: The Arabic is coherent, but الوصيف means a servant, a preadolescent boy, or a runner-up—not simply 'the young man': [Arabic Language Academy](https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/محرك-البحث/معجم/dic-19/الوصيف).

arabic: الرُّمَّانُ فَاكِهَةٌ مُفَضَّلَةٌ لَدَى الطِّفْلِ النَّحِيفِ، وَقَدْ أَعْجَبَهُ جِدًّا.
english: Pomegranate is a favorite fruit of the thin child, and he liked it a lot.
reason: Grammatical and plausible; the translation conveys the meaning accurately.

arabic: اِتَّصَلَ الْمُشَارِكُ السُّورِيُّ بِالْوَكِيلِ لِأَنَّ التَّأْشِيرَةَ إِلَى تُونِسَ كَانَتْ مَطْلُوبَةً.
english: The Syrian participant contacted the agent because the visa to Tunisia was required.
reason: A coherent explanation for contacting an agent; the translation is accurate.

arabic: غَسَلَتِ الْجَارَةُ الْمَلَابِسَ ثُمَّ نَظَّمَتْهَا فِي الْخِزَانَةِ، وَهَذِهِ طَرِيقَتُهَا الْمُعْتَادَةُ.
english: The neighbor washed the clothes and then arranged them in the closet; this is her usual way.
reason: Natural description of a household routine, accurately translated.

arabic: أَضَاءَ الْمِصْبَاحُ الزُّقَاقَ الْقَاتِمَ فَرَاحَ الصَّبِيُّ يَلْعَبُ بِأَلْعَابِهِ هُنَاكَ.
english: The lamp lit up the dark alley, so the boy went off to play with his toys there.
reason: A plausible scene. فراح يلعب means he began playing; 'went off to play' is acceptable here.

arabic: الْتَحَقَ الصَّبِيُّ بِالنَّادِي وَوَاظَبَ عَلَى الرِّيَاضَةِ فَتَطَوَّرَ، وَالْمُدَرِّبُ يَدْعَمُ مُسْتَقْبَلَهُ.
english: The boy joined the club and persevered at sports, so he improved, and the coach supports his future.
reason: Coherent and grammatical, though supporting someone's future is slightly abstract in both languages.

arabic: دَمَّرَتِ الْحَرْبُ بُيُوتًا عَدِيدَةً عَلَى الْجَبْهَةِ، لَكِنَّ الْأَطْفَالَ نَجَوْا.
english: The war destroyed many houses at the front, but the children survived.
reason: Natural description of wartime destruction and survival; accurately translated.

arabic: يَعْتَقِدُ الْعَبْدُ أَنَّ طَاعَةَ الْإِلٰهِ هِيَ سَبِيلُ السَّلَامَةِ وَالْغِبْطَةِ.
english: The servant believes that obeying God is the path to safety and joy.
reason: Plausible religious language; 'servant' and 'joy' appropriately convey العبد and الغبطة.

arabic: عَالَجَ الْمُتَخَصِّصُ الطِّفْلَ مِنَ الْجُدَرِيِّ فَشَفَاهُ، وَاخْتَفَتِ الْأَعْرَاضُ تَمَامًا.
english: The specialist treated the child for smallpox and healed him, and the symptoms disappeared completely.
reason: Grammatical and plausible in a historical narrative; the translation is accurate.

arabic: خَادَعَ اللِّصُّ السَّائِحَ وَغَيَّظَهُ، فَطَرَدَهُ السَّائِحُ مِنَ الْفُنْدُقِ وَوَجَدَ مِحْفَظَتَهُ.
english: The thief tricked and angered the tourist, so the tourist expelled him from the hotel and found his wallet.
reason: A plausible narrative sequence, with the actions accurately translated.

arabic: أَدْرُسُ الصَّوْتِيَّاتِ وَالْفِعْلَ فِي هَذَا الْمَقْطَعِ لِأَنَّ مُحْتَوَاهُ هَامٌّ.
english: I study phonetics and the verb in this passage because its content is important.
reason: Plausible in a language-study context; the translation matches the Arabic.

arabic: وَفْقاً لِلْبَرْنَامَجِ، التَّفَاعُلُ مُتَوَقَّعٌ مِنَ الطُّلَّابِ فِي الْحِصَّةِ الْمُقْبِلَةِ.
english: According to the program, interaction is expected from the students in the next class.
reason: Acceptable formal educational language, accurately translated.

arabic: اِنْبَسَطَ الْأَطْفَالُ فِي الْمِهْرَجَانِ بِصَوْتِ الطَّبْلِ وَالْبُوقِ، وَنَظَرُوا إِلَى الطَّاوُوسِ الْخَلَّابِ.
english: The children had fun at the festival with the sound of the drum and trumpet, and they looked at the charming peacock.
reason: A coherent festival scene; انبسط expresses enjoyment, and the translation is accurate.

arabic: اِعْتَصَرَ الوَلَدُ اللَّيْمُونَ وَخَلَطَ العِرْقسُوسَ بِالفَاكِهَةِ، ثُمَّ ذَاقَهُ وَكَانَ لَذِيذاً.
english: The boy squeezed the lemon and mixed the licorice with the fruit, then tasted it and it was delicious.
reason: Grammatical and plausible as a description of preparing and tasting a fruit drink.

arabic: الرَّجُلُ النَّبَاتِيُّ يَكْرَهُ الهَمْبَرْجَرَ وَالطَّاوُوقَ، لَكِنَّهُ يُحِبُّ السَّلَطَةَ جِدّاً.
english: The vegetarian man dislikes hamburgers and tawook, but he loves salad very much.
reason: A plausible statement about food preferences. 'Dislikes' is slightly weaker than يكره, but conveys the meaning adequately.

arabic: يَوْمَ الأَحَدِ جَهَّزَتِ الشَّغَّالَةُ المَنْسَفَ لِلاِسْتِضَافَةِ فَأَصْبَحَتْ مُتْعِبَةً.
english: On Sunday the maid prepared the mansaf for the hosting, so she became tired.
reason: مُتْعِبَةً means 'tiring' or 'exhausting,' not 'tired.' The intended word is مُتْعَبَةً.

arabic: تَوَقَّعَ الرَّئِيسُ نَزَاهَةَ الاِنْتِخَابِ وَقَبُولَ الخَلِيفَةِ فِي المَقَرِّ.
english: The president expected the integrity of the election and the acceptance of the successor at the headquarters.
reason: Formal and somewhat vague, but plausible in a political context involving an election and acceptance of a successor.

arabic: سَجَّلَ المُصَوِّرُ مَظْهَرَ الشَّاعِرِ: شُحُوبَهُ وَتَجْعِيدَةً عَلَى شَفَتِهِ.
english: The photographer recorded the poet's appearance: his paleness and a wrinkle on his lip.
reason: A plausible description of a photographer documenting someone's appearance; the translation matches.

arabic: طَالَمَا كَانَ المَلَاكُ مُخَلِّصاً فَلَا غَضَبَ فِي الفِرْدَوْسِ وَلَا خِيَانَةَ.
english: As long as the angel is sincere, there is no anger in paradise and no betrayal.
reason: مُخَلِّصاً means 'a savior' or 'a deliverer,' not 'sincere,' which would be مُخْلِصاً.

arabic: طَرَحَ الوَلَدُ لُغْزاً مُعَقَّداً فَحَيَّرَ بَاقِيَ الزُّمَلَاءِ وَأَصْبَحُوا مُفْحَمِينَ.
english: The boy proposed a complex riddle, which perplexed the rest of the colleagues and left them speechless.
reason: A coherent description of a difficult riddle leaving the others perplexed and speechless.

arabic: عَفْواً، هَاتِ جَوَازِي مِنَ الدُّولَابِ الآنَ، وَأَنَا مَمْنُونٌ لَكَ.
english: Excuse me, hand me my passport from the cupboard now, and I'm grateful to you.
reason: A natural request with an expression of gratitude; the translation is accurate.

arabic: قَفَزَ التِّمْسَاحُ إِلَى العِجْلِ فِي الزَّاوِيَةِ فَصَدَّتْهُ السُّلَحْفَاةُ المَاهِرَةُ.
english: The crocodile jumped at the calf in the corner, but the skilled turtle fended it off.
reason: Plausible in an animal fable or children's story, and accurately translated.

arabic: فِي السَّحَرِ أَيْقَظَ المَسْحَرُ الوَلَدَ الَّذِي سَهِرَ عَلَى الإِذَاعَةِ.
english: At dawn the pre-dawn caller woke the boy who had stayed up listening to the radio.
reason: The caller should be المُسَحِّرُ, not المَسْحَرُ. Also, السَّحَرِ means the time before dawn, rather than dawn itself.

arabic: هَاجَرَ زَمِيلِي فَكَاتَبْتُهُ، ثُمَّ اِتَّصَلَ بِي وَهُوَ يَرْغَبُ فِي العَوْدَةِ.
english: My colleague emigrated so I corresponded with him, then he contacted me wanting to return.
reason: Grammatical, coherent, and accurately translated.

arabic: عَانَتِ الفَتَاةُ العَزْبَاءُ مِنَ الوَحْدَةِ وَالخَجَلِ، ثُمَّ تَحَوَّلَ مِزَاجُهَا فَأَصْبَحَتْ مَبْسُوطَةً.
english: The single girl suffered from loneliness and shyness, then her mood changed and she became happy.
reason: A plausible description of a change in mood. مبسوطة is acceptable informal usage for 'happy.'
